title: SLO-aware token-credit orchestration and limiter outage mitigation
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: We need a distributed, SLO-aware token-credit allocator that gracefully handles limiter outages and regional failover without sharp user-visible drops. Primary goals are (1) preserve P95 latency and success SLOs for premium routes during transient limiter failures, (2) enforce global fairness for multi-tenant workloads, and (3) provide deterministic, observable fallback behavior when the primary quota service is degraded.

What we built so far (progress):
- Design doc: initial spec uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SLO-aware+Token+Credit+Orchestration (draft).
- Prototype: local simulation harness created (sim/slo-token-orch) that models soft-credit drains and lease regen under 20%/50%/80% failure modes. Sim results attached in the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4823.
- PoC service: token-orchestrator v0 runs as a sidecar in staging, implements soft credits per region, per-customer hard cap, and a probabilistic admission shim to smooth bursts. Deployed to staging-capacity-3 cluster (staging region eu-west-1) for evaluation.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Soft credits vs hard reservations: we chose a hybrid model where nodes pre-fetch soft credits up to a short TTL lease (30s) to absorb short bursts without contacting central control plane. Hard caps remain enforced centrally for long-running abuse. Trade-off: soft credits reduce latency but require robust reconciliation to prevent over-commit; we limit lease window and track per-lease generation IDs to simplify reconciliation.
- Probabilistic admission (p-drop) for fairness: instead of strict token queues, we apply a p-drop calculation that factors recent token usage and SLO priority to avoid head-of-line blocking across tenants. Trade-off: adds variance to per-request success but improves aggregate SLOs under overload.
- Circuit breaker hysteresis: when central limiter error rate or latency exceeds thresholds, we enter a 'degraded local mode' with conservative soft-credit allocation and stronger p-drop. We prefer hysteresis + cooldown over immediate full fail-open to avoid oscillations.
- Lease reconciliation strategy: implement periodic lease scans and an eventual correction path that uses delta reconciliation (not full resets) to minimize surprised requests. This avoids huge token revocations that would spike client errors.

Open risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Partitioned clocks/clock skew causing lease overlap -> mitigation: leases include monotonic generation IDs and node-local counters; system prefers last-writer-wins with bounded TTL to avoid double-issue beyond a small epsilon.
- Risk: Long network partitions may cause regional over-issuance -> mitigation: region-level backpressure signals and cross-region admission gating; automatic rollback to central-enforced hard caps when connectivity is restored.
- Risk: Observability gaps for degraded mode behaviors -> mitigation: new dashboard panels and synthetic checks (see monitoring section).

Monitoring, alerts, and SLOs:
- New metrics to emit: orchestrator.soft_credits_issued, orchestrator.lease_reconciliations, admissions.prob_drop_rate, admissions.p95_latency_ms, limiter.circuit_open_count, limiter.central_error_rate, limiter.override_mode_active.
- Dashboards: staging and prod dashboards created (Grafana links): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rlbSloTok/orchestrator-overview and a canary dashboard at https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/canary/rlb-slo-canary.
- Alerts: P0 alert when p95 latency for premium routes > 400ms for 3m or when central_error_rate > 1% for 5m. Operational runbook attached: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/token-orchestrator-degraded-mode.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit + integration tests for lease issuance, reconciliation, and p-drop behavior. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4823.
- Chaos tests: TP/sim harness to inject 10s-5m network blackout between region and central limiter; measure over-issuance and SLO impact.
- Canary rollout: start with non-critical tenant group in us-west-2 (1% traffic) -> 5% after 24h -> 25% after 72h -> full region. Canary stop criteria: error-rate increase > 2x baseline or premium-route P95 breach.

Implementation notes and follow-ups:
- Service components: token-orchestrator (sidecar), central-limiter-proxy, admission-shim library for SDKs. Admission-shim will offer a simple API: tryAcquire(tokens, priority) -> {granted, reason, lease_id}.
- Backwards compatibility: default mode is transparent (no-op) unless feature-flagged per-route via Console rollout.
- Ops: add a limiter-incident playbook and a KMS rotate checklist for service keys.

Recent reviews and feedback:
- PM review (Sofia Martinez): asked for clearer SLO mapping and a stronger canary stop condition for enterprise customers—added route-level SLO labels to the orchestration config.
- Design review (Alex Rao): requested we tighten lease TTL to 20s for routes with high QPS—compromise: configurable TTL per-priority; default 30s, premium 15-20s.
- Security review kickoff: ticket opened with Security (SEC-742). We need an HSM keywrap design for sidecar-to-central auth; blocker for Private deployments.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Finish security HSM integration spec and add to PR (owner: Priya Nair).
- Expand canary to eu-west-1 after smoke tests (owner: Liam Chen).
- Add synthetic long-tail latency test to CI harness (owner: QA).
- Draft customer communication for enterprise tenants on expected behavior during degraded mode (owner: PM).

Links: 
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/SLO-aware+Token+Credit+Orchestration
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4823
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/canary/rlb-slo-canary
- Runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/token-orchestrator-degraded-mode

Notes for reviewers: look at the reconciliation algorithm in pkg/orch/reconcile.go and the admission p-drop curve in pkg/admit/pdrop.go. We're prioritizing predictable SLOs for premium routes even if that means higher transient rejection for best-effort tenants. If this priority mapping is unacceptable, call out suggested mapping changes in comments.
